articles.headline: NFL Week 6: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 6.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第6週：日曜日の試合から得られた大きな収穫、疑問点、そしてファンタジー視点での考察
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの記者たちが、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えながら、全ての展開に反応します。第6週から得られた知見がこちらです。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars. 

Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made his much-anticipated Texans debut, but it was quarterback C.J. Stroud who was the star of this day as Houston was able to hold off the Jaguars in a thriller.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

HOU-JAX

Catch up on Thursday's game:

SEA-DEN

Houston 34, Jacksonville 31

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Texans

Can quarterback C.J. Stroud keep this hot start going? Even though Stroud did have an ill-timed interception that gave the Jaguars a chance late in the fourth quarter, he was stellar. The fourth-year quarterback is continuing to perform at an MVP level, but against the Jaguars, Houston needed him at his best -- and he delivered. He led the game-winning drive to cap a 306-yard, three-touchdown outing in his first London performance.

Trend to watch: The Texans' "elite" defense has been far from it. Coach DeMeco Ryans took over playcalling this week, but his unit allowed 31 points. It's the third time this season that the Texans have allowed at least 30 points. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: vs. Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Jaguars

Is it time for the Jaguars to fully unleash Travis Hunter on offense? They may need to. Hunter had his best offensive game of the season. He caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown after having just two catches for 17 yards in the first five games. The Jaguars needed him to step up because receiver Brian Thomas Jr. struggled, dropping two passes -- including one that would have given the Jaguars a chance to attempt a long field goal at the end of the first half. Thomas, who had an issue with drops last year, didn't play an offensive snap in the second half after playing 15 in the first. Hunter, with a bigger offensive workload, could make up for Thomas' struggles.

Trend to watch: The Jaguars are banged up at safety, with Antonio Johnson leaving the game with an ankle injury. They were already down Caleb Ransaw (IR) and went to Kaevon Merriweather, who was on the practice squad until he was signed to the active roster before last week's game. With the bye next week, the Jaguars need to get healthy and possibly make another move depending on how long Johnson is out. -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: vs. Colts (Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET)

articles.headline: Kyren Williams says Rams' inconsistencies on offense 'probably' due to role
articles.description: Asked why he thought the Rams' energy level was inconsistent from drive-to-drive Sunday, RB Kyren Williams said: "Probably because I'm not out there."
articles.headlineJa: カイレン・ウィリアムズ、ラムズの攻撃の不安定さは「おそらく」役割によるものと語る
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日の試合でラムズのエネルギーレベルがドライブごとに変動していた理由を問われたRBカイレン・ウィリアムズは、「おそらく、私がフィールドに出ていないからだろう」と答えた。
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- After the Rams dropped to 2-4 with an 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday, running back Kyren Williams was asked why he thought the team's energy level was inconsistent from drive-to-drive.

"I can't tell you, bro," Williams said. "Probably because I'm not out there."

Williams has shared the load at running back this season with 2024 third-round pick Blake Corum. On Sunday, he played 40 offensive snaps to Corum's 16. Williams had 10 carries for 50 yards and three catches for 17 yards. Corum had nine carries for 42 yards and two catches for 18 yards and a touchdown.

For the season, Williams has played 70% of the Rams' offensive snaps (287 of 410), Corum 28% (114 of 410). Williams also has played the third-most offensive snaps of any running back this season (only the Colts' Jonathan Taylor and Steelers' Jaylen Warren have played more).

When asked whether he thought he should be playing a higher percentage of snaps, Williams said, "I can't really call that.

"It's not on me, but I just think no matter what, we got to continue to have the energy."

The Cardinals, who closed as 13.5-point underdogs, pulled the biggest upset of the season based on point spread, according to ESPN Research, and became only the second double-digit underdog to win outright in the last two seasons.

Coach Sean McVay said the Rams cannot get out of their own way, with "critical" and "unforced errors," penalties and a lack of execution.

"We won't win a game unless we figure out how not to beat ourselves," he said. "... And so we have a lot to look at ourselves on and we have to be able to go back to the drawing board and figure out how we improve because like I just told you guys, we have to be able to not beat ourselves before we figure out how to even come away with some of the results. And it's not even good enough.

"There is nothing positive that I can say about today."

McVay said he didn't have an answer to why the Rams have so many self-inflicted wounds, noting, "A lot of different guys are taking their turn."

"I've continued to talk about it," he said. "We try to be able to harp on it and we've got to be able to figure it out. And I don't have those answers right now, otherwise it would've gotten fixed. ... That's what our narrative has been for this year.

"And we can't keep saying, 'Oh, we haven't done that before.' Well, this year we are doing it and so we have to be able to fix it, and it's my job to do that."

The Rams are now 2-4 in an NFC West division led by the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers, who play Monday against Washington. According to NFL NextGen Stats, the Rams have a 43% chance to make the playoffs.

The Rams are the fifth team in the last 50 seasons to enter a season as the outright Super Bowl favorites and lose at least four of their first six games, according to ESPN Research. None of the previous four reached the conference championship.

articles.headline: Cruel Achilles injury has killed the Ben Simmons comeback Australia was dying to see
articles.description: For the first time in years, Ben Simmons had given us a reason to believe. That's what made the news of his Achilles injury hit so heavily -- he'd started to answer a question that had followed him for half a decade, Olgun Uluc writes.
articles.headlineJa: 残酷なアキレス腱の怪我により、オーストラリアが切望したベン・シモンズの復活は絶たれた
articles.descriptionJa: 数年ぶりにベン・シモンズは期待させる根拠を示していた。だからこそアキレス腱の怪我のニュースは大きな衝撃を与えた。彼は5年間つきまとっていた疑問に答え始めていたと、オルグン・ウルク氏は記している。
articles.body:
For the first time in years, Ben Simmons had given us a reason to believe.

That's what made the news land so heavily. Because it wasn't just that Simmons had torn his Achilles; it was that it happened now, days before the NBA season, just as he'd started to answer a question that had followed him for half a decade.

Every Achilles tear is cruel, but this one felt slightly more unjust than most. For years, the knock on Simmons was that he didn't care enough. He was supposedly a gifted athlete who'd drifted on talent alone; someone who enjoyed the fruits of the game more than the game itself. This comeback was quietly dismantling that idea. He was returning from back injuries that very well should have been debilitating, which isn't something you just 'talent' your way back from that.

So, on the eve of the NBA season, that comeback being cut short by something out of his control was particularly jarring. It robs us of seeing whether the Australian with the greatest peak in the NBA, and someone who had the potential to be an all-time great, could return to that trajectory.

Given what Simmons hasn't done on a basketball court in recent years, it's worth reminding ourselves what he was. As a high school player out of Melbourne, he was the first Australian ever selected for the McDonald's All-American game, widely regarded as the premier exhibition in junior basketball in the U.S. He was the consensus No. 1 player in his class, winning the Naismith, Gatorade and Morgan Wootten national player of the year awards.

I sat with a then-18-year-old Simmons in the bowels of the United Center in Chicago in April, 2015 during McDonald's All American week. Cameras, recruiters, sneaker reps, and reporters filled every corridor, all waiting on the same handful of teenagers. We sat for an interview on the concourse of the arena. Shaquille O'Neal had just called him the best player in the world.

"People can say what they want but, at the end, I have to bring it," Simmons told me at the time.

For all intents and purposes, he did bring it. When he got to the NBA, as the No. 1 overall pick, LeBron James called him 'Young King'. That was apt because, with every big game from Simmons, three names were almost always attached: James, Oscar Robertson, and Magic Johnson.

Simmons became the only rookie ever to average at least 15 points, 8 rebounds, and 8 assists on better than 50% shooting; he was the first rookie since Robertson in 1961 to average 8 rebounds and 8 assists a game. He had 12 triple-doubles as a rookie, second only to Robertson's 26 and ahead of Magic.

Simmons was one of three rookies to reach 1,000 points, 500 rebounds, and 500 assists, alongside - guess who? - Robertson and Magic. There are too many to continue listing them, but it didn't take long for Simmons to earn three straight NBA All-Star selections (2019 to 2021), an All-NBA Third Team selection in 2020, All-Defensive First Team in 2020 and 2021, and the league's steals leader in 2019-20.

Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry.

Our NFL betting buzz file, with contributions from David Purdum, Doug Greenberg and others, aims to provide fans a look at the sports betting stories that are driving the conversation throughout each week of the season. 

Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds | Sports betting home | DraftKings 

Oct. 18: Cardinals pulls biggest upset of season, add to Rams' struggles

By David Purdum

The Los Angeles Rams won over the betting public in the offseason and kicked off the regular season as the clear-cut Super Bowl favorites. They haven't lived up to that billing so far, suffering a new low on Sunday.

The Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals as 13.5-point home favorites in the biggest upset of the season, point spread-wise. They are only the second double-digit favorite to lose in the last two seasons, joining the Green Bay Packers, who lost to the Carolina Panthers in Week 9 last November as 13.5-point favorites.

Arizona's upset shredded survivor pools around the nation.

The Rams were picked by more contestants in ESPN Survivor contests and also the top-selected team in the high-stakes survivor contests, Circa Survivor and Circa Grandissimo, in Las Vegas. Throw in the Indianapolis Colts' loss to the underdog and previously winless Tennessee Titans, and the Circa contests lost greater than 50% of the remaining entries.

The loss drops the Rams to 2-4 on the season, the same record as the Cardinals. The Rams are the second preseason Super Bowl favorite in the last 20 years to lose four of their first six games, per SportsOddsHistory.com. (The 2015 Seattle Seahawks also started 2-4 and would go on to lose in the divisional round of the playoffs.)

Los Angeles was favored to win the Super Bowl at 5-1 ahead of Week 1. No other team had Super Bowl odds shorter than 10-1. The Rams were +950 to win the Super Bowl on Sunday night at DraftKings, behind four teams.

More bets were placed and more money was wagered on the Rams to win the Super Bowl than any other team in the offseason at most sportsbooks.

Oct. 11: Who wants to win the NFC East?

By Doug Greenberg

Week 5 was one to forget for the NFC East, to say the least.

It started Thursday night when the Dallas Cowboys lost outright to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after closing as 8.5-point favorites, tied with four other games as the biggest upset of the season, according to DraftKings odds.

Not only were the Cowboys heavily backed on the spread and in moneyline parlays at multiple sportsbooks, they were also the most popular pick in both ESPN Survivor (40% of the remaining field) and the $1,000-per-entry Circa Survivor (2,554 entries, 42.8% of the remaining field). articles.headline: Cowboys returner KaVontae Turpin injures rib on opening kickoff vs. Packers
articles.description: Cowboys Pro Bowl returner Turpin suffered a rib injury on his opening kickoff return after he was tackled awkwardly.
articles.headlineJa: カウボーイズのリターナー、カヴォンテ・ターピンがパッカーズ戦のオープニングキックオフで肋骨を負傷
articles.descriptionJa: カウボーイズのプロボウル選出リターナーであるターピンが、オープニングキックオフのリターン中に不自然な形でタックルを受け、肋骨を負傷した。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- If the Dallas Cowboys are leave to Lambeau Field with a win, it will be without their Pro Bowl returner KaVontae Turpin.

On the opening kickoff, Turpin sustained a rib injury at his 25-yard return after he was tackled awkwardly. Turpin was examined on the sideline before heading to the locker room.

Running back Tyler Goodson replaced Turpin as the kick returner.

Turpin entered Sunday averaging 27.5 yards per kick return with a long of 48 yards and 11.1 yards on punts. Turpin has been named to the Pro Bowl three times -- 2022, 2024 and 2025 -- after joining the Cowboys from the USFL. He has had one kickoff return for a touchdown and one punt return for a score.

Offensively, Turpin has caught four passes for 39 yards and had two runs for 10 yards.

articles.headline: Kings guard Ben Simmons, 30, has torn Achilles tendon, will undergo surgery
articles.description: Kings guard Ben Simmons has sustained a torn Achilles tendon and will undergo surgery, the team announced Sunday, an injury that is likely season-ending for the 30-year-old veteran who authored an impressive training camp on short notice for Sacramento.
articles.headlineJa: キングスのガード、ベン・シモンズ（30歳）がアキレス腱断裂で手術へ
articles.descriptionJa: キングスのガード、ベン・シモンズがアキレス腱を断裂し、手術を受けることが日曜日にチームから発表された。急遽サクラメントに加入しトレーニングキャンプで素晴らしいパフォーマンスを見せていた30歳のベテランにとって、この負傷で今シーズンは絶望的となる可能性が高い。
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons has sustained a torn Achilles tendon and will undergo surgery, the team announced Sunday.

This is likely a season-ending injury for Simmons, 30, who authored an impressive training camp on short notice for Sacramento. The injury occurred during a live drill at Sunday's practice, the team said.

A three-time All-Star, Simmons agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million contract with the Kings on Sept. 4. Healthy at the time of the deal, the 6-foot-10, 240-pound guard impressed Kings general manager Scott Perry when he worked out for Perry in Miami and had an hourlong meeting in late August.

"I've faced challenges before that tested me mentally, physically and emotionally, and I've found a way through every single one of them," Simmons wrote in a statement posted on social media. "This injury is another chapter in my journey, not the end of my story."

Simmons also traveled to Sacramento last month to visit the Kings and impressed coach Doug Christie and other members of the basketball staff at the team's practice facility, where Simmons underwent an in-depth medical exam and conducted an on-court workout.

Over the following days, the Kings offered Simmons a contract with the expectation he would be a backup point guard for rookie Darius Acuff Jr. and play positions 1 through 5. Simmons was to serve as a high-upside reclamation project who still has years left in his prospective prime.

Simmons played two preseason games for the Kings, averaging 10.5 points in 17.5 minutes.

"It's never easy being away from the game I love, especially after everything it took to get back here," Simmons wrote. "But if there's one thing I've learned, it's that adversity doesn't define you. How you respond to it does."

articles.headline: Warriors' Stephen Curry 'fine' after tweaking right ankle in practice
articles.description: Steve Kerr said franchise superstar Stephen Curry is "fine" after he limped off the practice court with a right ankle issue.
articles.headlineJa: ウォリアーズのステフィン・カリー、練習中に右足首をひねるも「問題ない」
articles.descriptionJa: スティーブ・カー監督は、練習中に右足首の違和感でコートを後にし、足を引きずっていたチームのスーパースター、ステフィン・カリーについて「問題ない」と語った。
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry tweaked his right ankle during the team's open practice in San Francisco on Sunday night, limping to the locker room.

Coach Steve Kerr told reporters afterward that Curry avoided a major issue.

 

Curry was lined up against reserve guard De'Anthony Melton on the wing when he showed frustration after a slip and misstep, banging the basketball on the floor. Action stopped and Curry's teammates expressed immediate concern at his discomfort. Several staffers went down the tunnel to visit Curry, including Kerr.

"He's fine," Kerr said.

Curry missed 43 games last season, including 27 for persistent pain and swelling in his right knee. The Warriors have purposefully ramped up Curry's court work slower this season, lightening his practice time and minutes in the preseason. He turns 39 in March.

There is no immediate word on Curry's status, but a team source reiterated the ankle tweak is "not serious."

The Warriors open the season Wednesday night in Los Angeles against the Lakers.

articles.body:
With the preseason games coming to a close soon, the 2026-27 NBA season is less than a week away from tipping off.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 18

Suns' Ighodaro signs multi-year deal to stay in Phoenix

Phoenix Suns center Oso Ighodaro has agreed to a three-year, $29 million contract extension through the 2030-31 season, his agent Erika Ruiz of Primera Sports told ESPN.

The Suns will pick up Ighodaro's $2.5M team option for 2027-28, so the extension starts in 2028 and runs through 2031 for the franchise's 2024 second-round pick.

Simmons tears Achilles, out for the season

Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons tore an Achilles tendon at practice Sunday, sources told ESPN. Simmons, the 2016 No. 1 pick whom the Kings signed this offseason, was readying to play his first regular-season game since 2024-2025.

Oct. 16

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected

The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

articles.headline: Mou doesn't understand 'obsession' with elbow from Madrid's Güler
articles.description: José Mourinho claimed he hadn't seen "images" of an elbow by Arda Güler -- which saw no intervention from the referee -- in Real Madrid's 4-1 win over Sevilla.
articles.headlineJa: モウリーニョ、マドリードのギュレルによるエルボーへの『執着』を理解できず
articles.descriptionJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョは、レアル・マドリードがセビージャに4-1で勝利した試合において、審判の介入もなかったアルダ・ギュレルによるエルボーの「映像」は見ていないと主張した。
articles.body:
José Mourinho claimed he hadn't seen "any images" of an alleged elbow from Arda Güler -- which saw no intervention from the referee -- in Real Madrid's 4-1 win over Sevilla on Sunday, saying he didn't understand the "obsession" with the incident in his postmatch news conference.

Sevilla coach Luis Garcia Plaza was furious at the decision not to send off Güler for the first-half clash with Gerard 'Peque' Fernandez -- which occurred with the game tied at 0-0 -- saying his team was "denied the chance to play another game, 11 against 10."

However Mourinho suggested the discussion was an attempt by his counterpart to divert attention from the eventual 4-1 scoreline, after goals from Güler, Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande left Madrid six points behind leaders Barcelona heading into next weekend's Clásico.

"Nobody has been able to show me what they say happened," Mourinho said. "There aren't any images. I've asked for TV images, and for images from my staff who have the tactical camera, and I haven't been able to see any image of what's being talked about, what annoyed Luis [Garcia Plaza].

"Honestly, if one day something happens that benefits us, I'll have no problem in saying it. But I think the opposite will happen many more times, that's the tendency. I haven't seen anything. Until Saturday, if someone gets a clear and objective image to me of something I haven't seen -- and which my player says didn't happen -- I'll be there [to talk about it], but until then, nothing."

"Today we should have played with an extra man, from the 25th minute, 11 against 10," Garcia Plaza insisted. "I don't want to talk about the game after that. It's incredible. I saw it. Peque at halftime was saying 'he hit me.' It's a red card.

"Maybe we wouldn't have won, but we should have been playing 11 against 10, for 65 minutes. That's the summary of the game."

Madrid's victory at the Bernabéu allowed them to go into an important week -- with a Champions League game with RB Leipzig followed by the Clásico at Camp Nou -- with a run of three consecutive wins since the international break.

Mourinho made a number of key decisions in his team selection, bringing Güler into central midfield and starting Endrick after both impressed at Roma in midweek.

"I understand Luis [Garcia Plaza], with a team that loses 4-1," Mourinho said. "If the coach gets four or five questions about something which hasn't happened, that's fantastic for him.

"When it happened, I told [Real Madrid assistant coach] Pedro [Machado] I wanted to see it, but I couldn't see anything. Maybe there are other cameras, but until now, nothing."

"Have any of you seen it clearly?" Mourinho asked journalists. "That's why I don't understand the obsession with asking about it."

Mourinho said he also hadn't watched rivals Barcelona's 5-2 win at Real Betis a day earlier, which included a stunning Giovani Lo Celso goal for Betis being disallowed for an earlier handball.

articles.headline: Roberto De Zerbi on latest Tottenham training ploy: 'We removed phones' from meals
articles.description: Roberto De Zerbi has revealed phones were banned from meals during Tottenham's warm weather training camp in Marbella in his latest attempt to turn a vastly-assembled squad into a team.
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi has revealed phones were banned from meals during Tottenham's warm weather training camp in Marbella in his latest attempt to turn a vastly-assembled squad into a team.

Spurs committed more than £380 million ($505m) on new signings this summer with 10 players joining, but they will start Monday's home fixture with Coventry at the bottom of the Premier League with no wins from their opening six fixtures.

De Zerbi knows pressure will build if Tottenham fail to win, but will hope a midweek excursion to Spain can help turn frowns upside down in N17.

"We worked on the pitch, we stayed together -- we removed phones from breakfast, lunch and dinner to stay together because now it is like [phone] all the time," De Zerbi told a press conference.

"We had two or three important meetings speaking about football, our situation and how everyone has to take responsibility. And nothing more. There were some dinners just for the players, some dinners just for the staff.

"As a coach you understand you have to improve, you have to change the situation and you try to find all solutions.

"I already did this type of training camp two times with Marseille and it was a good solution. I spoke with the club, with Vinai [Venkatesham], with Johan [Lange], with the owner and together we took the decision, but it's nothing special.

"It's just to spend more time together because in pre-season we couldn't. We had many new players and players who came back from the World Cup. Three or four days together without family, putting the club at the top of their priorities, is normal and is good."

Asked if players were able to go out independently in Marbella, De Zerbi said: "Yes, with freedom. With no military rules. I love freedom."

Fit-again Dejan Kulusevski was part of the Tottenham squad in Spain along with James Maddison, who should face old club Coventry but is yet to start for Spurs since he damaged anterior cruciate ligaments in 2025 and Xavi Simons remains absent with the same injury.

"I am very close with Xavi Simons for example in this moment. I follow him step by step in his journey as an injured player. Like Maddison, because the management of Maddison is totally different. He is another special player and now is available to play," De Zerbi said.

- Kulusevski set to return to Tottenham squad after 526-day injury absence

"Kulusevski was a very important player, even last season when he was injured. It is a part of this job for the players, but at the same time can be a crucial moment to become better, to become stronger.

"You need to play many games to reach the best physical condition but there are players able to be important, even if they play 10, 15 or 20 minutes and James is one player like this.

"Right now he is ready to start the game, but I don't know if we will start with him. I'm waiting for that moment."

articles.headline: Yan Diomande, Kylian Mbappé lead Real Madrid rout of Sevilla
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé's brilliant double on Sunday helped Real Madrid prepare for next week's El Clasico with a 4-1 triumph over Sevilla at the Bernabeu.
articles.headlineJa: ヤン・ディオマンデとキリアン・エムバペが主導し、レアル・マドリードがセビージャを圧倒
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にキリアン・エムバペが鮮やかな2ゴールを決め、レアル・マドリードはベルナベウでセビージャに4-1で勝利し、来週のエル・クラシコに向けて弾みをつけた。
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé's brilliant double on Sunday helped Real Madrid prepare for next week's El Clasico with a 4-1 triumph over Sevilla at the Bernabeu.

The France striker finished off a fine team move in style to double Madrid's lead in the 37th minute after Arda Güler put the hosts ahead with a curling strike on the half hour.

Mbappé extended their advantage with a Panenka penalty after the break and although Manu Bueno scored a consolation goal, Yan Diomande soon fired home to wrap up the three points.

Victory comes just days after earning a stunning 4-3 comeback win over Jose Mourinho's former club Roma in the Champions League and ahead of a huge week for Los Blancos.

They return to European action against RB Leipzig on Wednesday before Sunday's trip to the Spotify Camp Nou, where Madrid take on LaLiga leaders Barcelona, who have started the domestic season with nine straight wins.

Madrid pulled off the one-sided win without the services of Vinícius Júnior, who is serving the first of a four-game ban for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba last weekend.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, keep James Wiseman ahead of opener
articles.description: The Knicks are waiving Bruce Brown and keeping James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: ニックス、ブルース・ブラウンを放出、ジェームズ・ウィズマンは開幕に向けて残留
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが報じたところによると、ニックスはレギュラーシーズン開幕を控え、ブルース・ブラウンを放出する一方で、ジェームズ・ウィズマンをロスターに留めることを決定した。
articles.body:
The New York Knicks waived Bruce Brown and will keep James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener.

Brown was one of several players on non-guaranteed deals vying for one of New York's final two available roster spots. Tony Bradley, Ochai Agbaji and Drew Eubanks were all also waived in recent days.

Wiseman appeared in all four of the Knicks' preseason games and impressed in 24 minutes vs. the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday, when he scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.

 

According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, the Knicks could have kept Brown and Wiseman, but because they are only $3.2 million below their self-imposed hard cap at the second apron, retaining both players would've been difficult.  

Wiseman, 25, will join Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond in New York's center rotation. The reigning NBA champions lost key reserve big man Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics this past summer via free agency.

The Knicks begin the NBA's regular season Tuesday, when they host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.headline: 76ers, needing frontcourt help, convert 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall to two-way contract
articles.description: The 76ers, dealing with injuries in the frontcourt, have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract.
articles.headlineJa: フロントコートの補強を必要とする76ers、7フィート6インチのタコ・フォールとツーウェイ契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: フロントコートでの怪我に悩まされている76ersは、センターのタコ・フォールをツーウェイ契約に切り替えた。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, the team announced Saturday.

Last month, the Sixers signed the 7-foot-6 center to an Exhibit 10 deal, and injuries to the frontcourt likely led to Fall getting this spot.

Ariel Hukporti, projected to be the Sixers' backup center, suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in the preseason. Center Adem Bona, potentially the next man up, has been sidelined with a foot injury, and Dominick Barlow has battled back soreness that kept him out of the preseason.

Fall hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season, when he was with the Cleveland Cavaliers. This will be his fourth season in the NBA. He played his first two in Boston with new Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Fall, 30, most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association.
